definition: Algorithm Selection maps a problem or dataset to an algorithm from a portfolio. In per-instance selection, meta-features and prior performance are used to choose the algorithm expected to minimize a task-specific cost.
intuition: Different datasets favor different algorithms; learn a mapping from dataset evidence to the best member of an algorithm portfolio.
mathematical_foundation:
$$
s: D \rightarrow A, \qquad s(D) = \arg\min_{a \in A} c(a,D)
$$

`D` is a dataset or problem, `A` an algorithm portfolio, and `c` the task-specific cost.
advantages: Can exploit dataset meta-features and prior benchmark results.
Uses a portfolio instead of assuming one algorithm wins on every dataset.
limitations: A portfolio cannot select an algorithm absent from the portfolio.
Meta-features and historical results may fail to transfer to a distribution-shifted dataset.
